2. The mouse is rough. (Fact 2)
3. The mouse sees the bald eagle. (Fact 3)

R2: If something is cold then it visits the mouse. ($Cold(x) \rightarrow Visits(x, Mouse)$)
R3: If something sees the mouse then it is cold. ($Sees(x, Mouse) \rightarrow Cold(x)$)
R4: If the mouse is cold then the mouse sees the bald eagle. ($Cold(Mouse) \rightarrow Sees(Mouse, Eagle)$) - Note: Fact 3 already says this, but this rule connects properties of the mouse to actions.
R5: If something is rough and it visits the bald eagle then the bald eagle sees the mouse. ($(Rough(x) \land Visits(x, Eagle)) \rightarrow Sees(Eagle, Mouse)$)

R7: If something is big and it visits the mouse then it is rough. ($(Big(x) \land Visits(x, Mouse)) \rightarrow Rough(x)$) - Irrelevant to target?

Now apply Rule R5 with $x = Mouse$:
If something (Mouse) is rough and it (Mouse) visits the bald eagle, then the bald eagle sees the mouse.
Condition met: Mouse is rough AND Mouse visits Eagle.
Conclusion: The bald eagle sees the mouse.

   Instantiating $x = Mouse$: Since the antecedent is true, the consequent $Sees(Eagle, Mouse)$ is true.
